Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the Horizon Financial Group Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. As a reminder, instructions for queuing up will be given at that time. Please note this event is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Sarah Thompson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Thompson:
Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to review Horizon Financial Group's results for the third quarter of 2024. With me this morning are John Reynolds, Chief Executive Officer; Michael Chen, Chief Financial Officer; Lisa Patel, Chief Risk Officer; David Kim, Chief Credit Officer; Elena Vasquez, Chief Technology Officer; and Robert Hayes, Chief Operating Officer.

Before we begin, let me remind you that some of the statements we will be making today are forward-looking. These statements are based on current expectations and assumptions and are subject to risks and uncertainties. Please refer to our SEC filings for a discussion of these factors.

I will now turn the call over to John Reynolds.

John Reynolds:
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. Horizon Financial Group delivered exceptional results in the third quarter, exceeding expectations and demonstrating the strength of our diversified business model with $1.2 trillion in assets.

Our key priorities for this year remain focused on accelerating revenue growth, improving profitability, managing risk effectively, investing in technology and innovation, enhancing customer experience, strengthening our brand, and delivering value to our shareholders.

Now, I'd like to provide some highlights. First, on net interest income trends, we achieved solid growth both year-over-year and quarter-over-quarter, reflecting disciplined balance sheet management. Second, our provision for credit losses was managed prudently, with builds driven by specific segments but offset by releases elsewhere. Third, revenue diversification efforts have meaningfully reduced our reliance on traditional interest income. Fourth, our asset sensitivity positions us well for rate changes, supported by robust interest rate risk hedging. Fifth, we're providing clear guidance for next quarter's NII and earnings. Sixth, operating expenses showed controlled growth amid strategic investments. And seventh, net interest margin expanded due to favorable yield dynamics and mix shifts.

I will now turn the call over to Michael Chen to discuss our financial results in more detail.

Michael Chen:
Thank you, John, and good morning. Horizon Financial Group reported net income of $2.8 billion for the third quarter, or $1.95 per share. Our results reflect strong revenue growth, disciplined expense management, and a healthy credit environment.

Net interest income increased 3.2% quarter-over-quarter to $4.8 billion from $4.65 billion in the second quarter, and a stronger 9.5% year-over-year from $4.39 billion in the third quarter of 2023. This outpaced many peers and highlights our asset-sensitive stance amid an inverted yield curve and easing deposit competition. Our net interest margin expanded 5 basis points sequentially to 3.52% and 27 basis points annually from 3.25%, marking three straight quarters of gains as asset yields rose faster than funding costs.

Quarter-over-quarter, the NII uptick came from 2% growth in average earning assets to $1.05 trillion, led by 4.1% expansion in commercial and industrial loans due to drawdowns in energy and manufacturing revolvers. Consumer loans like autos and credit cards grew 1.8%, boosted by digital lending partnerships that lifted originations 15%. Deposit betas eased to 45% from 52%, with $25 billion shifted to low-cost small business transactional accounts, holding deposit costs at 2.15%, up only 8 basis points. Securities yields improved to 4.1% on new Treasuries and agency MBS bought during the spring rate dip, while mortgage prepayments slowed to 12% CPR on our $80 billion residential book. Offsetting this somewhat were repricings on $10 billion in CDs at 4.8%, in line with industry lags behind the 5.25-5.50% Fed funds rate.

Year-over-year, the 9.5% NII rise beat mid-single-digit peer gains like those at Wells Fargo and PNC, powered by 6.2% loan growth to $750 billion, including 11% in C&I for data center capex amid AI demand. Mortgages held at $15 billion annualized, with purchases up from Sun Belt home price gains. Deposits rose 5% to $900 billion, with core DDAs up 4% at 28% mix and 1.2% cost, creating a 150 basis point repricing advantage over deposits' 110 basis point rise.

Regionally, our Southeast franchise led with 12% NII growth from Florida and Texas commercial real estate like multifamily and logistics. Midwest markets were flat sequentially but up 7% annually on auto finance. Asia-Pacific jumped 15% in local currency via our DBS joint venture on trade finance and SOFR swaps, though Europe dipped 2% from ECB cuts narrowing spreads to Euribor plus 120 basis points.

To keep this going, we've rolled out the Horizon Edge digital deposit platform, adding $18 billion in savings at 4.2% APYs and improving our loan-to-deposit ratio to 83%. We're hedging 40% of our $150 billion fixed-rate loans with swaps to secure over 4% yields ahead of 25-50 basis point Fed cuts next year, and sold $5 billion in non-core CRE to redeploy into C&I.

Turning to net interest margin more closely, it hit 3.52% this quarter, up 15 basis points from 3.37% last quarter and 28 basis points from last year. Earning asset yields rose 25 basis points to 5.20%, with C&I at 6.15% on SOFR-linked loans averaging 5.35%, and consumer segments adding tailwinds from 7.2% auto yields. Securities lagged slightly but benefited from duration cuts to 3.8 years. Southeast yields exceeded the national average by 40 basis points on CRE demand.

Liability costs climbed 40 basis points to 1.68%, tempered by a 45% cumulative deposit beta below peer averages. Transaction accounts rose 20 basis points to 1.25%, time deposits 65 to 3.80%, with new high-yield savings at 4.75% APY drawing $2.5 billion digitally. Wholesale funding trimmed to 8% of mix helped. The NIM bridge shows asset yield gains and loan mix shifts outweighing deposit drag.

On provisions for credit losses, we recorded $1.2 billion, up 15% sequentially from $1.04 billion but flat year-over-year. This added $450 million to our allowance, reaching $18.5 billion or 1.45% of loans, with 320% coverage of non-performers, competitive with JPMorgan and Wells Fargo.

CRE drove 55% or $660 million, with office and multifamily PDs up 20 basis points to 2.8% from vacancies at 19.5% and Sun Belt refi stress, though industrial stayed under 1.5%. Consumer released $150 million as auto delinquencies fell 25 basis points to 1.8% on a $120 billion book, with cards at 3.2% below industry norms. CIB added $450 million from leveraged deals with higher LGD at 42%. Macro overlays weighted downside GDP at 1.8%, inflation 2.6%, and Fed funds at 525 basis points.

Year-to-date PCL is $3.6 billion, below last year's $3.9 billion, with charge-offs at 65 basis points. US PCL up 12% on CRE, Europe down 5%, Asia up 20% from China property but offset by India.

Our CECL uses PD-LGD-EAD models over 36 months, with logistic regressions on 200 variables, updated collateral haircuts like 55% office LGD, and five scenarios. AI early warnings from Palantir flagged 30% more issues early, data lakes added alt data for 92% accuracy, and we de-risked $5 billion CRE.

Revenue diversification has shifted non-interest income to 42% of total revenue at $9.8 billion, up 22% year-over-year, growing 3x faster than NII and adding 150 basis points to 14.2% ROTE. Wealth and asset management fees hit $4.2 billion, up 28%, with $2.8 trillion AUM from $120 billion inflows; ESG funds grew 35% to $450 billion, robo-advisors boosted cross-sell 18%. Transaction banking fees rose 24% to $2.9 billion on $4.2 trillion payments, embedded APIs with Stripe-like partners, and blockchain cuts to seconds. Capital markets added $1.7 billion on M&A and trading.

This lowers volatility, expands fee margins to 65 basis points, and supports CET1 at 12.8%. Targets include 45% non-interest by 2026 via GenAI, BaaS, and APAC growth.

Asset sensitivity shows +5.8% NII or $285 million for +200 basis points, with 68% variable loans resetting quickly; EVE drop of 1.9% for -200 bps within limits. Duration gap at +0.85 years. We've added $12 billion pay-fixed swaps, securitized autos, and ML beta forecasts.

Operating expenses rose 4.2% year-over-year to $12.8 billion, flat sequentially, improving efficiency to 57.8%. Compensation up 6.8% on talent and variables, tech up 14.5% on cloud/AI saving $250 million run-rate, compliance up 8.2% on Basel/DORA. Branch closures cut occupancy, marketing shifted digital.

For Q4 guidance, NII of $2.55-2.60 billion implies 1-3% growth at 3.48-3.52% NIM assuming one Fed cut; EPS $1.52-1.62, PCL 25-35 basis points.

Our capital ratios remain strong at CET1 12.8%, well-positioned for growth.

Lisa Patel:
Thank you, Michael. From a risk management perspective, we are closely monitoring commercial real estate pressures, deposit outflows, and geopolitical FX swings. We are taking proactive steps like AI monitoring and hedging to mitigate these risks and maintain a strong risk profile.

David Kim:
Good morning. Our credit quality remains exceptionally strong with non-performing loans at 0.45% and net charge-offs at 65 basis points. We are actively managing our loan portfolio, particularly CRE at 12% with strict LTVs, and remain confident in navigating the economic environment. Specifically, the performance of our commercial and industrial portfolio has been strong.

Elena Vasquez:
Thank you. I'd like to provide an update on our technology initiatives. We are making significant progress on our digital transformation, including the launch of Horizon Edge and AI fraud tools which have seen rapid customer adoption, reducing losses by $80 million year-to-date and boosting efficiency across origination and monitoring.

Robert Hayes:
Good morning. We are focused on operational excellence and driving efficiency across the organization. Key initiatives include cloud migrations and branch optimizations, which are contributing to improved productivity, $250 million in projected savings, and a sub-58% efficiency ratio.

Operator, we are now ready to open the line for questions.

Operator:
Ladies and gentlemen, instructions for queuing up. Our first question comes from Jennifer Lee with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Jennifer Lee:
Good morning. Can you provide further insights into NII trends, especially regional dynamics and forward guidance?

John Reynolds:
Thanks, Jennifer. As Michael detailed, our NII grew robustly with QoQ and YoY gains led by C&I and deposit shifts. Southeast strength and Asia-Pacific trade finance were highlights, and we're guiding 2-4% QoQ growth in Q4 with NIM stable, supported by our variable-rate exposure.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Patel with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

David Patel:
What are your plans for revenue diversification going forward?

Michael Chen:
Great question, David. We've reduced NII reliance to 58%, with non-interest up 22% YoY from wealth fees, payments, and capital markets. Plans include GenAI wealth tools, BaaS scaling to $10 trillion embedded lending, and APAC to 25% mix, targeting 45% non-interest by 2026 for resilient earnings.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Maria Gonzalez with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Maria Gonzalez:
How are you managing provisions for credit losses amid CRE stress?

Lisa Patel:
Thanks, Maria. Our $1.2 billion PCL reflects targeted builds in CRE and CIB, offset by consumer releases, using advanced CECL with AI warnings and alt data. We've de-risked $5 billion CRE, keeping ACL at 1.45% and coverage 320%, with Q4 at $1.1-1.3 billion expected.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Chris Wong with Bank of America. Please go ahead.

Chris Wong:
Can you discuss the performance of your commercial real estate portfolio?

David Kim:
Absolutely, Chris. CRE at 12% of loans performed well overall, with industrial steady and office multifamily driving provisions from PD rises, but strict underwriting and sales keep us resilient versus peers, aligned with our strong overall credit metrics.

Operator:
There are no further questions at this time. I'd like to turn the conference back over to John Reynolds for any closing remarks.

John Reynolds:
Thank you for your interest in Horizon Financial Group. We appreciate you joining us today. We look forward to speaking with you again next quarter.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.

Provision for credit losses: drivers and methodology
Asset sensitivity and interest rate risk management
NII and earnings guidance for the next quarter
Operating expenses: trends and key drivers

aspect_summary.Revenue diversification initiatives and: Non-interest income 42% of revenue ($9.8B, +22% YoY, 3x NII growth), adding 150bps to 14.2% ROTE; from wealth/AUM fees ($4.2B +28%, $2.8T AUM), transaction banking ($2.9B +24%), capital markets ($1.7B); initiatives include Horizon Edge platform ($18B deposits), ESG/robo-advisors, embedded APIs/blockchain, GenAI, BaaS, APAC growth targeting 45% non-interest by 2026.
aspect_summary.Asset sensitivity and interest rate risk: +5.8% NII (+$285M) for +200bps shock, 68% variable loans resetting quickly, EVE -1.9% for -200bps, duration gap +0.85 years; managed via 40% hedging of $150B fixed loans with swaps (securing >4% yields), $12B pay-fixed swaps, auto securitizations, ML beta forecasts.
aspect_summary.NII and earnings guidance for the next q: Q4 NII $2.55-2.60B (1-3% QoQ growth, NIM 3.48-3.52% assuming one Fed cut); EPS $1.52-1.62; PCL 25-35bps; 2-4% QoQ NII growth reaffirmed.
aspect_summary.Operating expenses: trends and key drive: OpEx +4.2% YoY to $12.8B, flat QoQ, efficiency ratio 57.8%; driven by compensation (+6.8% on talent/variables), tech (+14.5% on cloud/AI, $250M run-rate savings), compliance (+8.2% on Basel/DORA), offset by branch closures, digital marketing shift.
aspect_summary.NIM analysis: factors influencing change: NIM +5bps QoQ/+27bps YoY to 3.52%; earning asset yields +25bps to 5.20% (C&I 6.15%, autos 7.2%, securities 4.1%, duration 3.8yrs); liability costs +40bps to 1.68% (deposit beta 45% < peers, transaction 1.25%, time 3.80%) but tempered by low-cost deposit shifts ($25B small business), loan mix shifts outweighing funding drag.
